newsitem.title: USA: ABC chief aims to revive TV network.
newsitem.headline: ABC chief aims to revive TV network.

text.p: ABC Inc President Robert Iger said on Tuesday he intended to focus in coming years on restoring the company's television network to its past glory.

"No other ABC asset has greater potential impact on our performance, and its ability to enhance our related businesses is extraordinary," Iger told shareholders of Walt Disney Co at the company's annual meeting here.
Disney acquired ABC for $19 billion last year.
Iger, who has been at ABC for 23 years, said the company was concentrating on strengthening its prime time line-up and adding more events and distinctive programs to its schedule.
ABC dominated TV ratings in the United States until a few years ago when rival NBC leaped ahead with a slew of hit comedies and popular dramas, such as "ER" and "Law and Order".
Iger said fixing the network will take time, but its affiliation with Disney provided the company with a wealth of creative talent.

Later this year, Disney plans to bring back the "Wonderful World of Disney" program on Sunday nights, a program geared to families that will feature network premiers for some of Disney's most successful films.
Iger said ABC planned to expand overseas with cable channels like the Disney Channel and ESPN, its all sports network.
ABC also wants to buy more radio and television stations, but will not get into a bidding frenzy, he said.
"The fear of consolidation will not cause us to mimic others who are paying prices which we believe to be too high to create shareholder value." he said.
